Responded by rolling back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. First rollback attempt was a partial failure (halted after us-east due to orchestrator error); retry completed the rollout to all regions. Service confirmed healthy on v2.3.0 in us-east, us-west, and eu-west with error rate back to ~0.2%. Follow-up: investigate root cause in v2.3.1 before any re-attempted rollout, and review the orchestrator error that interrupted the initial rollback.

trace.final:
Done. Here's a summary of what happened and what I did:

**Diagnosis:** checkout-api was running v2.3.1 (the latest deploy) in all production regions, failing health checks with an ~18% error rate. The most recent release that was healthy in production was **v2.3.0**.

**Rollback:** I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions. The first attempt was a partial failure — it halted after us-east due to an orchestrator error, leaving regions mixed. I verified current state, retried the rollback, and it completed successfully. Confirmed the service is now **healthy** on v2.3.0 in us-east, us-west, and eu-west, with error rate back down to ~0.2%.

**Incident:** Opened a SEV2 incident (INC-0001) for checkout-api describing the failure, the rollback actions (including the partial-failure and retry), and follow-up items: root-causing v2.3.1 before any re-deploy attempt, and reviewing the orchestrator error that interrupted the initial rollback.

Note: I did not need change-manager approval since v2.3.0 was previously healthy in production.
